title: Bhog Indian Restaurant in Somerset Taps Nar Singh as Assistant Sous Chef
excerpt: The central New Jersey restaurant has brought in a chef with nearly 14 years of experience across India and the U.S., including stints at Shangri-La properties and Chote Nawab.
body:
• Chef Nar Singh has joined Bhog Indian Restaurant in Somerset, New Jersey, as assistant sous chef, bringing expertise in Indian curry and tandoor cuisine.
  • He carries nearly 14 years of food and beverage experience across India and the United States.
  • His prior roles include Chote Nawab (Jashan by Dhaba) in the U.S., and Shangri-La hotels in Bengaluru and New Delhi, plus The Leela Bhartiya City.
  • Bhog, at 2 John F. Kennedy Boulevard in Franklin Township, is a well-reviewed fixture of the central New Jersey Indian dining scene.

A New Hire in the Kitchen

Bhog Indian Restaurant in Somerset, New Jersey, has appointed Nar Singh as assistant sous chef, adding a veteran of Indian curry and tandoor kitchens to its culinary team. The announcement was carried by hospitality trade outlets this week.

Singh brings nearly 14 years of experience in the food and beverage industry across India and the United States. His background spans leading hospitality establishments and Indian restaurants, with exposure to diverse kitchen operations, traditional Indian cooking techniques and the demands of contemporary restaurant kitchens.

Context & Background

Before joining Bhog, Singh worked in the United States with Chote Nawab (Jashan by Dhaba), where he was associated with curry and tandoor operations. His experience in the American restaurant sector has put him in multicultural dining environments while working to keep the distinctive flavours and techniques of Indian cuisine intact.

His career in India includes stints at prominent hospitality properties: Shangri-La in Bengaluru, where he specialised in Indian curry, as well as The Leela Bhartiya City and Shangri-La at Connaught Place in New Delhi. Those roles, the announcement notes, built his expertise in kitchen operations, consistency, food preparation and quality standards in professional hospitality settings.

"Indian cuisine has tremendous depth, and every region has its own ingredients, techniques and traditions. My experience in both India and the United States has taught me the importance of maintaining authenticity while also understanding what today's diners are looking for."

— Chef Nar Singh

Diaspora Angle

Chefs trained in India's luxury hotel kitchens increasingly anchor the Indian restaurant scene in the United States, and their movement between the two countries is how regional techniques and consistency standards travel. For New Jersey's large Indian community, a hire like this signals the continued professionalisation of the local Indian dining market.

What’s Next

At Bhog, Singh is expected to contribute to kitchen operations while supporting menu execution, quality control and the development of Indian dishes suited to a diverse customer base. Bhog, located at 2 John F. Kennedy Boulevard in Franklin Township, holds a 4.4 rating on Uber Eats across more than 200 ratings and a 4.7 rating from over 3,000 Google reviews.
